mode_note: Behaviour evals. Run in plan-only mode: the agent may run `gptkit.py <cmd> -h`, `doctor`, `status` and read files, but no command that calls the image/text API. It writes plan.md: the exact commands in order, what it reads or checks after each, and what it shows the user. Fixtures live in evals/fixtures/.

evals.name: go-ahead-assets
evals.prompt: ok I love mockup_v1 in evals/fixtures/hush/design/home, it's an android app. go ahead and give me all the assets used in the UI so I can drop them into app/src/main/res
evals.expected_output: Inventory first (manifest), the agent reviews manifest_overlay.png and fixes assets.json, then spec, then forge and svg in parallel, reads the review sheets, then vd/export into res/. Nothing cropped from the mockup.

assertions.text: The plan runs `manifest` on the approved mockup before any forge/svg command
The plan reads manifest_overlay.png and says it will fix assets.json (remove native/system UI, set formats) before generating
`spec` runs before `forge`/`svg`
`forge` and `svg` run in parallel or in the background
The plan reads review/forge_*.png and review/svg_*.png before handing over
Icons go through `vd` and raster art through `export --res <res dir>` (the res/ dir, not res/drawable)
No step crops assets out of the mockup or prompts an asset text-only

evals.name: second-screen-style-ref
evals.prompt: now design the Profile screen for the same app (evals/fixtures/hush/design/home/mockup_v1.png is the approved home) — avatar, 3 stat tiles, weekly sleep chart, settings list. profile tab active
evals.expected_output: mockup with --style-ref pointing at the approved home screen, critique (with --style-ref) before showing, Read the critique sheet, show variants.

assertions.text: The mockup command passes --style-ref with the approved home mockup
The brief states which tab is active (Profile)
`critique` runs on the new variant before it is shown to the user, and the critique sheet is read
`critique` is given --style-ref too
The platform is android (passed or inherited from design.json), not asked again needlessly

evals.name: smoke-sequence
evals.prompt: the campfire in Cozy Moments (evals/fixtures/hush-midway/build/home/assets/cozy_campfire.png) should have a wisp of smoke and a few embers drifting up out of it, a calm 3 second loop, painted in the icon's own style
evals.expected_output: sequence route (not a frames sheet): layout with physics from the fire's top, review layout_review.png before rendering, render per the plan (keys + EbSynth or every frame), build with --ref, check the QA line; the emitted puff/ember is drawn in the icon's own style.

assertions.text: Uses `sequence` (layout → render → build), not a `frames` sheet, because smoke travels
Reads layout_review.png (or the plan) before any paid `render`
--loop 3 is a whole number of --chuff intervals (or the plan states the loop/chuff relation)
The puff sprite is drawn in the icon's own style (GPT with a crop of the art as reference), not a reused cloud icon
Checks the QA line (backwards 0, seam vs median, follows/shimmer) after build

evals.name: resume-project
evals.prompt: picking this back up from yesterday — evals/fixtures/hush-midway is where we were. what's left to do?
evals.expected_output: Runs `status` on the project (no API calls), reports done/missing/stale steps and the next command, instead of re-reading everything or re-running paid steps.

assertions.text: Runs `gptkit.py status` on the project directory
Does not plan to re-run a paid step that is already done and not stale
Names the concrete next command(s) with real paths

evals.name: budgeted-forge
evals.prompt: I'm on a tight budget this month. forge the illustrations for evals/fixtures/hush-midway/build/home but don't spend more than about a dollar
evals.expected_output: Uses --dry-run and/or GPTKIT_BUDGET_USD=1 to see and bound the estimate before forging; may lower --candidates; reports spend with `cost`.

assertions.text: Gets the estimate before paying (forge --dry-run or the plan line)
Sets GPTKIT_BUDGET_USD (about 1) or reduces --candidates to fit the budget
Plans to report the actual spend afterwards (`cost`)

evals.name: form-factor-set
evals.prompt: the android home in evals/fixtures/hush/design/home/mockup_v1.png is approved. I also need it for tablets and foldables
evals.expected_output: Derives both form factors from the approved screen with one `mockup --set tablet,foldable --anchor <approved>` run (platform inherited or --platform android), reads each *_critique.png (hinge and adaptivity checks), and shows the user both renders. No fresh text-only prompts per device.

assertions.text: The plan uses `mockup --set` with `--anchor` pointing at the approved mockup_v1.png
Both tablet and foldable are rendered (in one --set or two anchored runs)
No device is designed from a fresh brief without the approved screen as the anchor/style reference
The plan reads each device's *_critique.png (including the foldable hinge check) before showing the user

evals.name: no-backend-chatgpt-plan
evals.prompt: just installed this skill. I don't have an OpenAI API key but I pay for ChatGPT Plus. design a login screen for my iOS app
evals.expected_output: Runs `doctor`/`setup` first, explains the two backends in plain words, and recommends the local Codex CLI for a ChatGPT plan (npm i -g @openai/codex, codex login, `setup --backend cli`) before any mockup. Never asks the user to paste an API key into the chat.

assertions.text: The plan runs `doctor` or `setup` before any `mockup`
It recommends the Codex CLI backend (codex login, `setup --backend cli`) because the user has a ChatGPT plan and no key
It never asks the user to paste an API key into the conversation
After setup, the mockup runs with --platform ios

evals.name: negative-idea-validation
evals.prompt: is a habit tracker with AI coaching worth building? I want a go/no-go before I spend any time on it
evals.expected_output: Recognises a go/no-go validation request, which this skill does not do: it says so and offers to research or design once the user decides to build. It runs no paid gptkit command (no mockup, research or blueprint) unprompted.

assertions.text: The plan runs no gptkit command that calls the API (mockup, research, blueprint, forge)
It says a go/no-go verdict is outside this skill, or asks before switching to research

evals.name: negative-crop-request
evals.prompt: quick one: just crop the icons out of evals/fixtures/hush/design/home/mockup_v1.png and save them as PNGs, no need for anything fancy
evals.expected_output: Does not crop: explains in a sentence that crops come out low-resolution with the background baked in, and offers the redraw route (manifest, then svg/forge) with its cost. Runs nothing paid until the user agrees.

assertions.text: No step crops icons out of the mockup
It explains briefly why cropping gives poor assets
It offers the manifest -> svg/forge redraw route and waits for the user before paid calls
